findings.issue: markRetry возвращает 'pending' | 'dead' | 'noop', тогда как ADR §4.2 фиксирует сигнатуру как Promise<'pending'|'dead'>. Расхождение контракта с дизайном.
findings.suggestion: Расширение АДДИТИВНОЕ и корректное — 'noop' честно обрабатывает гонку, когда строку уже забрал параллельный диспетчер (UPDATE WHERE state='dispatching' → 0 строк). Это улучшение, а не дефект; реальный диспетчер (outboxDispatcher.ts:109) ветку 'noop' уже учитывает. Привести бы формулировку ADR §4.2 к коду при следующем касании дока — не блокирующе.

findings.issue: runOutboxOnce берёт now из Date.now() напрямую, тогда как PostgresOutboxStore инжектит Clock (NF-5). Лёгкая несогласованность с дисциплиной инъекции часов.
findings.suggestion: На тестируемость не влияет (юнит-тесты подменяют сам store, а не время диспетчера), на прод-поведение тоже — now здесь лишь фильтр pendingBuckets(now). Если захочется детерминированно тестировать окно available_at на уровне диспетчера — проброс Clock в opts. Не блокирующе.

transactional_integrity_focus.enqueue_idempotency_race: ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING + SELECT-back is race-safe: each enqueue is a single auto-commit pool.query (no surrounding tx holding the winner uncommitted), so the losing INSERT observes a COMMITTED conflicting row and the SELECT-back always finds it — no null window. partial-unique predicate exact (tenant_id leading, WHERE NOT NULL) verified live.
transactional_integrity_focus.backward_compat: enqueue 4th param optional; externalWorker.ts additive (idempotencyKey validated ≤255, optional); InMemoryJobStore gained parity (byIdempotencyKey Map). FF-9 confirmed: pgJobStore diff is enqueue-only, complete/fail bodies byte-identical to T-0114.
transactional_integrity_focus.outbox_atomicity: enqueueInTx(client, row) runs on the CALLER's pg.PoolClient and opens NO transaction of its own → domain mutation + outbox INSERT commit/rollback together (AC-8). Contract is enforced by the API shape (method REQUIRES a PoolClient arg) — a consumer cannot accidentally split them across connections.
transactional_integrity_focus.two_phase_dispatcher_T0116_parity: Phase-1 SECURITY DEFINER outbox_pending_buckets(p_before) → exactly 2 cols (tenant_id, pending_count), no GUC, search_path pinned (choros, pg_catalog), REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC + EXECUTE-only to choros_app — verified live via pg_proc.prosecdef/proconfig/proacl. Phase-2 claimBatch: UUID-validated SET LOCAL, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. 1:1 with T-0116 next_due_buckets/fetchAndFire.
transactional_integrity_focus.no_rollback_invariant: State transitions monotonic-forward; no SQL path emits dispatched→pending or attempts decrement (claimBatch only state='pending'; markDispatched/markRetry only WHERE state='dispatching'). BUILD claim re-verified live (probe_d).

test_infra.singleClientPool: Honest pattern: wraps one GUC-scoped PoolClient as a pg.Pool so store methods calling both this.pool.query and this.pool.connect land on the same connection that already SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id inside an open tx — reproduces prod 'method executes on a GUC connection'. getOutboxHealth/pendingBuckets tests correctly use migratorPool (BYPASSRLS, no GUC), exactly the prod role semantics for those two cross-tenant/health methods.
test_infra.no_file_parallelism: Global package.json fitness:db change is justified (D-056, shared-PG races); did NOT mask concurrent defects — AC-12 parallel-claimBatch SKIP-LOCKED test runs concurrent assertions INSIDE its file and passes; CI time unaffected (6.53s).
test_infra.prod_guc_for_outbox_methods: getOutboxHealth/pendingBuckets run on a pool WITHOUT GUC by design — mirrors pre-existing getTimerHealth/createTimerStore (T-0116) verbatim. Relies on DATABASE_URL being migrator/BYPASSRLS-roled, identical to timer health precedent — a consistent deployment assumption, not a T-0062 regression.
